question: Will more Iranian planes be grounded abroad, yes or no?

lines.text: Istanbul has seized an Iranian jet. The debt: three million euros.
Officers boarded the Caspian Airlines Boeing 737 just before take-off, passengers already on board.
Everyone was ordered off and taken back to the terminal.
A Turkish court ordered the seizure, over unpaid bills for services at Istanbul Airport.
lines.note: Creditor: ACM Temsil Gozetim; debt about €3m ($3.4m)

lines.text: Caspian Airlines says it faces temporary operational restrictions, due to an administrative issue in Turkey.
lines.note: Caspian Airlines statement via Turkish Minute, The New Arab

lines.text: The airline said the plane would return to Iran on Tuesday.
lines.note: Caspian Airlines via Turkish Minute, The New Arab

lines.text: It comes as Iran's airlines are squeezed. The US has sanctioned twenty-seven Iranian airlines this month.
The UAE, Oman and Iraq have banned Iranian airlines.
Euronews says flights at Tehran's main airport have roughly halved, to about 41 a day.
lines.note: Euronews: international flights down from 80 to 90 a day to about 41

lines.text: Turkey has not banned them, but The New Arab says Mahan Air halted Turkey flights at Ankara's request.
And Iraq says Iraqi Airways will restart Iran flights in October, under a special US exemption.
lines.note: Iraqi Transport Ministry, 29 Sep 2026; no US confirmation (The National)

lines.text: One jet, one debt. Will more Iranian planes be grounded abroad, yes or no?

Turkey's foreign ministry did not respond (Turkish Minute, New Arab)
